anomalies.observed: The net /NET0148 contains only the anodes of D10, D35, and D49. There is no supply, pull-up, or driver on this net. The LED cathodes are tied through resistors to open-collector/open-drain style status outputs, but the common anode node is floating.
anomalies.expected: Indicator LEDs need a complete current path: their anodes should be connected to a positive supply (e.g. +3V3/+5V) or otherwise driven high so that the cathode-side switches can sink current and light the LEDs.
anomalies.impact: D10, D35, and D49 cannot light because their anodes have no positive supply path. Any status indication intended from these LEDs would be absent or behave differently from the intended design.

anomalies.observed: R71 is given value "24k" and is simulated as 24k, but its MPN and description fields specify a 24Ω part: MPN "FRC0805J240TSD" and description "... 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor ...".
anomalies.expected: The schematic value, BOM MPN, and part description should agree. For this high-impedance Ethernet/common-mode clamp network, a 24k resistor is consistent with the circuit role; a 24Ω resistor would heavily load VOUTP/VOUTN and change the clamp behavior.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R71") (value "24k") (footprint "Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric") ... (field (name "MPN") "FRC0805J240TSD") ... (field (name "Description") " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS"))

anomalies.impact: If assembled from the MPN/description rather than the schematic value, R71 would be 24Ω instead of 24k. That would load the Ethernet common-mode/protection node, alter the zener/MOSFET clamp biasing, and could affect Ethernet protection or signal behavior.

parsed.summary: The netlist contains a clear floating LED anode net (/NET0148) that prevents D10, D35, and D49 from functioning, and R71 has a schematic/SPICE value of 24k that conflicts with its BOM MPN/description of 24Ω.
